mainTopic: Checking family lineage (יוחסין) before marriage: the clean status of בבל, signs of good lineage, and the borders of בבל
overview: The amud opens by settling a contradiction between two clauses of an earlier source. Before a marriage we check a family's lineage, but we do not force apart a couple who are already married without proof of a problem. רב יוסף rules that anyone who speaks like a Babylonian may marry without a check, though nowadays swindlers fake the accent, so we stay careful. Two stories follow. In the first, זעירי avoids marrying רבי יוחנן's daughter, and the גמרא explains that עזרא left בבל pure 'like fine flour.' In the second, עולא tells רב יהודה that nobody can be sure of his own lineage, using פסוקים from איכה and עמוס. עולא then gives a practical test: the one who goes quiet first in a quarrel comes from the better family. רב agrees that silence is the sign of lineage in בבל, and that ongoing feuds hint at a hidden flaw. The amud ends by ranking the lineage of different lands and mapping the borders of בבל along the Tigris and the Euphrates.

steps.title: Two clauses, two situations: marrying versus separating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves a contradiction between two clauses of an earlier source. One clause deals with allowing a man to marry, and the other deals with taking away a wife he already has.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the source is talking about letting him marry a woman. There, it is talking about taking a woman away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a contradiction raised just before this section. It says the two clauses are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a man of uncertain lineage marries, we are strict and check his family first. Once he is already married, בית דין will not force them apart unless there is real proof of a problem. So the clauses do not argue; they cover different stages.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there: a formula for saying two sources deal with different cases
To let him marry a woman
To take a wife away from him (force a separation)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one clause is more lenient about lineage itself. The standard of proof is simply different before the marriage than after it.

phrases.english: Here – it is about marrying a woman to him,
there – it is about removing a woman from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן – לְהַשִּׂיאוֹ אִשָּׁה, כָּאן – לְהוֹצִיא אִשָּׁה מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised in the text just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא of each clause to a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses seemed to give opposite rulings about a family of unclear lineage.
steps.terutzMaskana: One clause is about permitting a new marriage, where we check first. The other is about breaking up an existing marriage, which needs proof.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a Babylonian speaker may marry without a check
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that anyone whose speech is Babylonian may marry without a lineage investigation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Anyone whose speech is Babylonian, we let him marry a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a practical rule. If a man talks like someone from בבל, we assume he comes from there, and we let him marry without checking his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Families from בבל were considered to have clean lineage. So a person's Babylonian speech works as a sign of where he comes from, and that is enough to skip the investigation.

keyTerms.meaning: His speech, the way he talks (his language and accent)
We allow him to marry a woman
Babylonia, considered to have very clean lineage

phrases.english: Rav Yosef says:
Anyone whose speech is Babylonian,
we marry a woman to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כֹּל שֶׁסִּיחָתוֹ בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical rule about who needs a lineage check before marrying
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who speaks like a Babylonian is presumed to be from בבל and may marry without his lineage being checked.

steps.title: Nowadays, because of swindlers, we are careful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב יוסף's rule: now that there are swindlers, we worry even about people who speak like Babylonians.
steps.simpleTranslation: But nowadays, when there are swindlers, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רב יוסף's rule. Since cheaters may fake a Babylonian accent, speech alone no longer proves anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself was never wrong. It worked because a Babylonian accent used to be a reliable sign. Once people began faking it to avoid a check, the sign stopped being trustworthy, so we go back to checking.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned (so we do not rely on it)

phrases.english: But nowadays, when there are swindlers,
we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב יוסף's rule for later times
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Now that people fake a Babylonian accent, we no longer rely on speech alone to skip a lineage check.
steps.whatToRemember: A Babylonian accent once counted as proof of good lineage. Once swindlers began faking it, we stopped relying on it.

steps.title: זעירי avoids רבי יוחנן and carries him across the water
steps.stepSummary: A story: זעירי, a Babylonian, kept avoiding רבי יוחנן, who wanted him to marry his daughter. Once, on a trip, זעירי carried רבי יוחנן across a puddle on his shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי kept avoiding רבי יוחנן, because רבי יוחנן kept telling him, 'Marry my daughter.' One day they were walking on the road and came to a puddle of water. זעירי put רבי יוחנן on his shoulders and carried him across.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the idea that Babylonian lineage is especially clean. This step sets the scene for רבי יוחנן's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי was from בבל and would not marry into a family from ארץ ישראל. Still, he honored רבי יוחנן greatly as a Torah teacher and carried him through the water. That contrast is what triggers the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A puddle or pool of water
He lifted him onto his shoulders

phrases.english: Ze'eiri was avoiding
Rabbi Yochanan,
since he would say to him: Marry my daughter.
One day they were walking along the way,
they arrived at a puddle of water,
he lifted Rabbi Yochanan onto his shoulders
phrases.notes: 'He' is זעירי.

phrases.english: and was carrying him across.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְעֵירִי הֲוָה קָא מִישְׁתְּמִיט מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story about the belief that Babylonian lineage is cleaner
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זעירי, a Babylonian, refused to marry רבי יוחנן's daughter from ארץ ישראל, yet he honored רבי יוחנן as a Torah scholar.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: our Torah is fit but our daughters are not?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges זעירי: you honor our Torah, so why are our daughters not good enough for you? What is your reasoning?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our Torah is fit, but our daughters are not fit? What are you thinking?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן points out that זעירי is being inconsistent and asks him to explain himself. The question 'what are you thinking' sets up the next step, where רבי יוחנן guesses זעירי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge plays respect for Torah against refusal to marry. If people from ארץ ישראל are worthy enough to teach Torah and be carried with honor, why treat their families as having doubtful lineage? It is worded as a question but works as an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your reasoning? What are you thinking?

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here רבי יוחנן is the one speaking to זעירי.

phrases.english: Our Torah is fit,
and our daughters are not fit?
What is your reasoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן reacts to זעירי's show of honor by challenging his refusal
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's refusal to marry a woman from ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is inconsistent to treat the Torah of ארץ ישראל as worthy of honor while treating its families as unfit for marriage.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rejects the 'ten lineages' reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן guesses that זעירי relies on the משנה that ten lineage groups came up from בבל. He rejects it: not all the pure families left בבל, so not all the flawed ones did either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of what we learned in the משנה, that ten lineage groups came up from בבל, such as כהנים and לויים: did all the כהנים, לויים and ישראלים go up? Just as some of these stayed behind, some of those stayed behind too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן puts forward the reason he thinks זעירי has, and then knocks it down. He argues that בבל is just as mixed as ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says groups with problematic lineage, like ממזרים, came up from בבל with עזרא and settled in ארץ ישראל. זעירי seems to conclude that only בבל is clean. רבי יוחנן answers that the people who went up were only part of each group, so flawed families must also have stayed behind in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possible reason, usually to reject it)
Is that to say...? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: If we say it is from what we learned in a mishna:
Ten lineage groups came up from Babylonia,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on קידושין 69a. It lists the groups that came up with עזרא, including some with flawed lineage.

phrases.english: priests, Levites –
is that to say that priests, Levites and Israelites
all came up?
Just as some of these remained,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the families with clean lineage, and 'those' in the next line are the ones with flawed lineage.

phrases.english: some of those remained as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִדִּתְנַן: עֲשָׂרָה יוּחֲסִין עָלוּ מִבָּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's own question by guessing זעירי's reason and rejecting it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the משנה of the ten lineages makes בבל cleaner than ארץ ישראל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only part of each group went up from בבל. Some flawed families must therefore also have stayed behind, so בבל is no cleaner.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן missed רבי אלעזר's teaching about Ezra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן did not know רבי אלעזר's teaching: עזרא did not leave בבל until he made it like pure fine flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: This escaped him, what רבי אלעזר said: עזרא did not go up from בבל until he made it like clean fine flour, and then he went up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in and defends זעירי. It says רבי יוחנן's argument falls apart because he did not know רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן assumed flawed families stayed behind in בבל. רבי אלעזר teaches that עזרא took all the flawed families up with him, leaving בבל pure 'like fine flour.' So the people left in בבל really did have clean lineage, and זעירי's caution makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It escaped him (he did not know or remember it)
The leader who brought the Jews back from בבל to ארץ ישראל
Clean fine flour, an image of complete purity

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, עזרא took the families with flawed lineage up with him. So the families left in בבל had clean lineage, which explains why זעירי avoided marrying into ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the background to the whole sugya: why בבל was considered the gold standard of clean lineage, and why a Babylonian accent could once replace a family check.

phrases.english: This escaped him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יוחנן; the גמרא is now commenting on his argument.

phrases.english: that which Rabbi Elazar said:
Ezra did not go up from Babylonia
until he made it like clean fine flour,
phrases.notes: He took all the families with flawed lineage with him, so only clean families were left behind.

phrases.english: and then he went up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns רבי יוחנן's rejection and defends זעירי's position
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוחנן's claim that flawed families stayed behind in בבל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן did not know that עזרא purposely took all the flawed families with him, leaving בבל completely pure.

steps.title: עולא visits and sees רב יהודה's son is unmarried
steps.stepSummary: עולא comes to רב יהודה's house in פומבדיתא and notices that his son רב יצחק is grown but not married.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא arrived in פומבדיתא at the house of רב יהודה. He saw that רב יצחק, the son of רב יהודה, was grown up and still not married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. This line sets the scene for the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is argued yet. We only learn the situation: a grown son who has not married. In the next lines we find out why, and the reason is connected to the topic of clean lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in בבל

phrases.english: Ulla arrived in Pumbedita
at the house of Rav Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: חַזְיֵיהּ לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: He saw Rav Yitzchak, the son of Rav Yehuda,
who was grown up and not married.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אִיקְּלַע לְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא לְבֵי רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second story on the theme of worrying about lineage, after the story of זעירי and רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה is grown and unmarried.

steps.title: עולא asks why the son is not married
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks רב יהודה why he has not found a wife for his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to רב יהודה: Why doesn't the master marry off his son to a woman?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא asks a direct question: why haven't you married off your son? This sets up רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arranging a marriage for a son was the father's job. So the question is really asking what is holding רב יהודה back.

phrases.english: He said to him:
What is the reason
that the master does not marry off
a woman to his son?
phrases.notes: "The master" is a polite way of saying "you," speaking to רב יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָא מַנְסֵיב לֵיהּ מָר אִיתְּתָא לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the situation described in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב יהודה has not arranged a marriage for his son.

steps.title: רב יהודה is unsure where to find clean lineage
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that he does not know which family he can safely marry into.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: Do I know where I can take a wife for him from?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that he is stuck because he cannot be sure which families have clean lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry here is about יוחסין, the purity of a family's lineage. רב יהודה is afraid of marrying his son into a family that might have a hidden flaw.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Do I know from where I should marry him off?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is afraid of lineage flaws and does not know which family is safe.

steps.title: עולא argues that none of us knows our own lineage
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that we cannot be sure of our own lineage either. We might descend from women who were attacked during the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Do we ourselves know where we come from? Maybe we come from those about whom it is written: "They ravished the women in Zion, the maidens in the cities of Judah."
steps.whatsHappening: עולא pushes back. If you are worried about other families, you should be just as worried about yourself, because nobody's family history is certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא turns רב יהודה's worry back on him. During the חורבן, Jewish women were attacked by enemies. Any of us could descend from them. So refusing to marry out of doubt makes no sense when our own lineage carries the same doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (a word that opens a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Is that to say that we know
where we come from?
Perhaps we are from those about whom it is written:
"They ravished the women in Zion,
the maidens in the cities of Judah."
phrases.notes: איכה 5:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ אֲנַן מִי יָדְעִינַן מֵהֵיכָא קָאָתֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's reason from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reason for delaying his son's marriage: fear of a flawed family.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our own lineage is just as doubtful, since we may descend from women attacked by enemies. So the worry cannot justify refusing others.

steps.title: Even if such a child is כשר, we might come from immoral people
steps.stepSummary: עולא heads off a reply. Even if a child born from a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is כשר, we might descend from the sinners described in עמוס. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains who they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that when a non-Jew or a slave lives with a Jewish woman the child is כשר, then maybe we come from those about whom it is written: "Who lie on beds of ivory and stretch out on their couches." And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: These are people who urinate naked in front of their beds.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא expects רב יהודה to say that the first worry is no problem. So he raises a second worry: maybe we descend from the corrupt people described in the נביא עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first doubt fails if you hold that a child of a non-Jew or slave with a Jewish woman is fully כשר. עולא therefore needs a source that points to a real flaw. He cites the פסוק in עמוס about people stretched out on their couches. At first it is explained by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא as crude, immodest behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introduces an expected reply)

keyTerms.term: נׇכְרִי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jew or slave who lives with a Jewish woman
the child is כשר (has acceptable lineage)

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying the child of a non-Jew is כשר as a final ruling. He is only saying: even if you hold that view, there is still another doubt.

phrases.english: And if you would say

phrases.aramaic: נׇכְרִי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: a non-Jew or a slave who lives with a Jewish woman,
the child is כשר,
then perhaps we are from those about whom it is written:
"Who lie on beds of ivory
and stretch out on their couches."
phrases.notes: עמוס 6:4

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
These are people who urinate
naked in front of their beds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נׇכְרִי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ahead of time a reply to step 11 and adds a second, stronger source of doubt.
steps.kashyaTarget: An expected defense: that descent from attacked women causes no lineage flaw.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even granting that defense, we may descend from the sinners in עמוס 6:4. This sets up a reading of that פסוק.

steps.title: רבי אבהו mocks the mild reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו objects. Could such a minor fault really earn the punishment of going first into exile?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו scoffed at this: If so, is this what is written: "Therefore now they shall go into exile at the head of the exiles"? Because they urinate naked in front of their beds, they "shall go into exile at the head of the exiles"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו rejects רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's explanation. The punishment in the next פסוק is far too harsh for such a small fault.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A few פסוקים later, עמוס says these people will be the first to go into exile. רבי אבהו reasons that a punishment that severe must fit a severe sin. Crude behavior near the bed does not fit. So the explanation must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: they will go into exile at the head of the exiles

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu scoffed at it:
phrases.notes: Literally "he cursed it." He means he strongly mocked that explanation.

phrases.english: If so, is this what is written:
"Therefore now they shall go into exile
at the head of the exiles"?
phrases.notes: עמוס 6:7

phrases.english: Because they urinate
naked in front of their beds,
"they shall go into exile at the head of the exiles"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְגַדֵּף בַּהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation of the פסוק given in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading of עמוס 6:4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The harsh punishment in עמוס 6:7 does not match such a minor fault.

steps.title: רבי אבהו explains the sin as wife-swapping
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the people in the פסוק swapped wives. Their beds were fouled with seed that was not their own, which would produce ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבהו said: These are people who eat and drink together, push their beds together, swap their wives with each other, and foul their couches with seed that is not theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives his own explanation of the פסוק. The sin was wife-swapping, which is serious enough to explain the harsh exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading fits both פסוקים. "Stretched out" (סרוחים) is read as "fouling" (מסריחים) the beds with another man's seed. It also completes עולא's argument. Children of these unions with married women would be ממזרים, and any of us could descend from them. So no family can be fully sure of its lineage.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's point stands. Since our ancestors may include ממזרים from the wife-swapping sinners in עמוס, nobody can be sure of perfectly clean lineage. So refusing to marry out of doubt is unreasonable.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין זֶה עִם זֶה,
phrases.english: These are people who eat and drink with each other,
and push their beds together,
and swap their wives with each other,
and make their couches foul
with seed that is not their own.
phrases.notes: This is how he reads "סרוחים" in the פסוק. Children from married women swapped this way would be ממזרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading from step 12 with a new explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sinners of עמוס 6:4 swapped wives, so their children could be ממזרים. This makes everyone's lineage doubtful.

steps.title: So what are we supposed to do?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks עולא how anyone can find a safe family to marry into, if nobody's family line can be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to עולא: What should we do?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reacts to עולא's warning with a practical question. This sets up עולא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא has just shown that anyone might come from a flawed line, even ourselves. So רב יהודה is not arguing back. He is asking for a working method to judge families.

keyTerms.meaning: What should we do? How should we act?

phrases.english: He said to him: What shall we do?
phrases.notes: רב יהודה is speaking to עולא, picking up right after עולא's warning that our own lineage is unsure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to עולא's warning that everyone's lineage is uncertain by asking for a practical solution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical way to know which families have clean lineage.

steps.title: Watch who goes quiet first in a fight
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers: follow the silence. In ארץ ישראל, when two people quarrel, the one who goes quiet first is judged to come from the better family.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Go by silence. That is how the people of the West, ארץ ישראל, check. When two people quarrel with each other, they watch which of them goes quiet first, and they say: This one comes from the better family.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a practical test for lineage. He points to a custom from ארץ ישראל: the one who stops fighting first has the better family line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family records may not be reliable, so עולא uses behavior as the clue. Being able to hold back and go quiet in a fight is treated as a sign of a clean family line.

keyTerms.meaning: the people of the West, meaning the people of ארץ ישראל
of good lineage, from a clean family

phrases.english: He said to him: Go after the silence,
phrases.notes: Now עולא is answering רב יהודה.

phrases.english: like the way the people of the West examine:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִינְּצוּ בֵּי תְרֵי בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
phrases.english: when two people quarrel with each other,
they see which of them is first to go silent,
and they say: This one is of finer lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question with a practical test.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Judge lineage by who goes quiet first in a quarrel, as is done in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of a quiet nature as a mark of good lineage, which the next steps build on.

steps.title: In בבל too, silence shows good lineage
steps.stepSummary: רב states that in בבל, being silent is itself the sign of good lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The silence of בבל is its lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives his own statement that the silence test works in בבל too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא described a custom of ארץ ישראל. רב adds that in בבל, a person's silence is what counts as proof of good lineage, so the same test applies there.

phrases.english: Rav says: The silence of Babylonia
is its lineage.
phrases.notes: He means that in בבל, the way to check someone's lineage is to see if he goes quiet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends עולא's silence test to בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In בבל, silence is the sign of good lineage.

steps.title: But רב checked a family's lineage directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב visited the house of בר שפי חלא and examined them. Wasn't he checking their family records, not their silence?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב came to the house of בר שפי חלא and checked them. Wasn't he checking their lineage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב's statement using a story about רב himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If silence alone is the test in בבל, why would רב need to examine a family? It looks like he was checking their lineage the usual way, which would go against his own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge
son of a vinegar strainer, a family's name

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אִיקְּלַע רַב לְבֵי בַּר שָׁפֵי חַלָּא
phrases.english: But Rav arrived at the house of the son of a vinegar strainer
and examined them. Was it not into their lineage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement from רב's own actions.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that silence is the lineage test in בבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself examined a family, which suggests he checked their lineage directly and did not rely on silence.

steps.title: He was checking their silence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רב was checking their silence. He told the examiners to see whether the family went quiet in a fight.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, he was checking their silence. This is what he told them: Check whether they go quiet or don't go quiet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what רב was really checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story does not go against רב. His examination was exactly the silence test: he sent people to see how the family acted in a quarrel.

phrases.english: No, into their silence.
This is what he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: בְּדוּקוּ אִי שָׁתְקִי אִי לָא שָׁתְקִי.
phrases.english: Examine whether they become silent or do not become silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reading the story differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב examined the family's lineage records directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב examined whether the family went quiet in a quarrel, which matches his rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Both עולא and רב treat going quiet in a quarrel as a sign of good lineage, and רב's visit to בר שפי חלא was a check of exactly that.

steps.title: Two people who keep feuding
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that when two people keep fighting, one of them has a hint of a flaw in his lineage, and he is kept from joining the other through marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If you see two people fighting with each other, there is a trace of unfitness in one of them, and he is kept from joining the other.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement about lineage begins. Fighting between two people is treated as a hint that one of them has a flawed family line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight itself is a sign. Because one side has a hidden flaw, he is stopped from marrying into the other's family, and the fight is how that happens.

keyTerms.meaning: a trace of unfitness, a hint of a flaw in lineage
to join, here meaning through marriage

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
If you see two people
who are feuding with each other,
there is a trace of unfitness in one of them,
and he is not allowed
to join one with the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אִם רָאִיתָ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from quarrels as a test of silence to quarrels as a sign of a flaw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ongoing fighting between two people hints at a lineage flaw in one of them, which keeps them from joining through marriage.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a contradiction of the silence test. There, the one who goes quiet first shows good lineage. Here, the ongoing fight itself is a sign that one side has a flaw.

steps.title: Two families that keep feuding
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the same about two families: when they keep fighting, one has a hint of a flaw and is kept from joining the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If you see two families fighting with each other, there is a trace of unfitness in one of them, and it is kept from joining the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a parallel statement about whole families instead of two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב spoke about two people. רבי יהושע בן לוי applies the same idea to whole families: a feud between families hints that one of them has a flawed line.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
If you see two families
feuding with each other,
there is a trace of unfitness in one of them,
and it is not allowed to join the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: אִם רָאִיתָ שְׁתֵּי מִשְׁפָּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement that widens רב's idea from two people to two families.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ongoing fighting between two families hints at a lineage flaw in one of them.

steps.title: רב's health chart of the lands
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא סבא in the name of רב describes the lineage of four lands: בבל is healthy, מישון is dead, מדי is sick, and עילם is dying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא סבא said in the name of רב: בבל is healthy. מישון is dead. מדי is sick. עילם is dying.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement compares the lineage of different lands using the picture of a person's health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל is healthy, meaning its families are clean. מישון is dead, meaning its families are all flawed. מדי is sick and עילם is dying; the next steps explain the difference between those two.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa the Elder says in the name of Rav:
Babylonia is healthy. Mishon is dead.
phrases.notes: Healthy means its lineage is clean; dead means its families are all flawed.

phrases.english: Media is sick. Eilam is moribund.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: בָּבֶל – בְּרִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement ranking the lineage of different lands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל has clean lineage, מישון is fully flawed, מדי is sick, and עילם is dying.

steps.title: What's the difference between sick and dying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'sick' (מדי) is different from 'dying' (עילם).
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between the sick and the dying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of two of רב's words. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'sick' and 'dying' sound like a mixed state between healthy and dead. The גמרא wants to know what actually separates them.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference between

phrases.english: And what is the difference between the sick and the moribund?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a clearer meaning of two terms in רב's statement.

steps.title: Most sick people live, most dying people die
steps.stepSummary: Most sick people recover, but most dying people die. So most of מדי has clean lineage, but most of עילם is flawed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Most sick people go on to live, and most dying people go on to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference: it is about which way the majority goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick person usually gets better, so 'sick' מדי means most of its families are clean. A dying person usually dies, so 'dying' עילם means most of its families are flawed.

phrases.english: Most sick people go on to life,
most of the moribund go on to death.
phrases.notes: So in מדי most families are clean, and in עילם most families are flawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by explaining both terms through the majority rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sick means most survive, so most of מדי is clean. Dying means most die, so most of עילם is flawed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's chart: בבל is fully clean, מישון is fully flawed, מדי is mostly clean, and עילם is mostly flawed.

steps.title: How far does בבל reach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the borders of בבל are for lineage purposes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until where is בבל?
steps.whatsHappening: Since בבל was called 'healthy' in lineage, the גמרא now asks how far בבל stretches. This question sets up the answers of רב and שמואל that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that בבל has clean lineage only helps if we know which towns count as בבל. The first question is about its width.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonia, the land called 'healthy' for lineage

phrases.english: Until where does Babylonia extend?
phrases.notes: He means: which areas count as בבל for the 'healthy lineage' rule from the earlier step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the statement that בבל is 'healthy' by asking where its borders are.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The borders of בבל for lineage purposes.

steps.title: רב and שמואל name two rivers
steps.stepSummary: רב says בבל reaches the river עזק; שמואל says it reaches the river יואני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: until the river עזק. שמואל said: until the river יואני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל each name a different river as the edge of בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא draws the line at a different river. Families living inside that line count as having clean lineage, like the rest of בבל.

phrases.english: Rav said: Until the River Azak,
and Shmuel said: Until the River Yo'ani.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: the river עזק. שמואל: the river יואני.

steps.title: How far north along the Tigris?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far בבל reaches going upward (north) along the Tigris river.
steps.simpleTranslation: Upward along the Tigris, until where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about a different direction: north along the Tigris. This sets up the next answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the width, the גמרא checks each direction separately. 'Upward' means upstream, which is northward.

keyTerms.meaning: Until where (Aramaic form of עד היכן)

phrases.english: Upward along the Tigris, until where?
phrases.notes: 'Upward' here means going upstream, which is northward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the width of בבל to its northern edge on the Tigris.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The northern border of בבל along the Tigris.

steps.title: רב says בגדא and אוונא; שמואל says מושכני
steps.stepSummary: רב says the border is at בגדא and אוונא; שמואל says it is 'until' מושכני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: until בגדא and אוונא. שמואל said: until מושכני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל give their northern borders on the Tigris.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's word 'until' sounds like מושכני itself is outside בבל. That wording is what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: Rav said: Until Bagda and Avna.
And Shmuel said: Until Mushekanei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: בגדא and אוונא. שמואל: מושכני.

steps.title: Isn't Mushekanei part of Babylonia?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: he himself said elsewhere that מושכני has lineage like the heart of בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is מושכני not included? But רבי חייא בר אבא said in שמואל's name: מושכני is like the גולה for lineage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל seems to contradict himself. Here 'until מושכני' sounds like it is left out, but elsewhere he says מושכני is fully kosher for lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is aimed at the wording 'until.' If 'until' means 'not including,' it clashes with שמואל's other statement, quoted by רבי חייא בר אבא, that מושכני is like the גולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The exile; the heartland of Babylonian Jewry

phrases.english: And is Mushekanei not included?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba say that Shmuel said:
Mushekanei is like the exile with regard to lineage!
phrases.notes: 'The exile' means the main Jewish towns of בבל, whose lineage is clean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Until' implies מושכני is excluded, yet שמואל elsewhere says מושכני is like the גולה for lineage.

steps.title: Until and including מושכני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל meant 'until מושכני, and מושכני itself is included.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: until מושכני, and מושכני is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the contradiction by reading שמואל's 'until' as including מושכני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in שמואל's ruling changes; only the meaning of 'until' is clarified. Now both of his statements agree that מושכני is kosher for lineage.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's border on the northern Tigris goes up to and includes מושכני.

phrases.english: Rather: Until Mushekanei, and Mushekanei is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until מושכני' meant מושכני was outside בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Until' includes מושכני, matching שמואל's other statement.

steps.title: How far south along the Tigris?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far בבל reaches going downward (south) along the Tigris.
steps.simpleTranslation: Downward along the Tigris, until where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the southern border on the Tigris. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Downward' means downstream, which is southward. Each direction gets its own answer.

phrases.english: Downward along the Tigris, until where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the northern edge on the Tigris to the southern edge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The southern border of בבל along the Tigris.

steps.title: Until Lower אפמייא
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל says the southern border on the Tigris is אפמייא תתאה (Lower Appamya).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל said: until Lower אפמייא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל gives the southern border: the town called Lower אפמייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'Lower' tells us there is more than one town with this name. The גמרא explains that next.

keyTerms.meaning: אפמייא, the name of a town

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל: עַד אַפַּמֵיָיא תַּתָּאָה.
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel said: Until Lower Appamya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל: עַד אַפַּמֵיָיא תַּתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The southern border on the Tigris is Lower אפמייא.

steps.title: Two towns named אפמייא
steps.stepSummary: There are two towns called אפמייא, upper and lower, a פרסה apart. One has kosher lineage and one does not, and they keep away from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two towns called אפמייא, one upper and one lower. One is kosher and one is flawed. Between them is a פרסה. They are strict with each other and do not even lend each other fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds background: there are two towns called אפמייא. One has kosher lineage, the other flawed, and the people keep strictly apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the towns are only a פרסה apart, their lineage is different. They refuse to lend each other even fire, so that no closeness forms that could lead to marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A פרסה, a unit of distance (about 4 מיל)

phrases.english: There are two Appamyas:
one upper and one lower,
one kosher and one flawed,
and between one and the other is a parasang,
and they are strict with one another,
and they do not even lend fire to one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב שמואל had to say 'Lower' אפמייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two towns called אפמייא a פרסה apart; one has kosher lineage, one flawed, and they keep apart.

steps.title: How to remember which one is flawed
steps.stepSummary: A memory sign: the flawed אפמייא is the one that speaks the מישון dialect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Your sign for the flawed one: it is the one that speaks the dialect of מישון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a trick to remember which אפמייא is flawed: the one whose people talk like people from מישון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 22) מישון was called 'dead' in lineage. So the town that speaks מישון's dialect is the flawed one.

phrases.english: And your sign for the flawed one:
it is the one that speaks the Mishon dialect.
phrases.notes: מישון is the land called 'dead' for lineage back in step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a memory sign to the description of the two towns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flawed אפמייא is the one that speaks the מישון dialect.

steps.title: How far north along the Euphrates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far בבל reaches going upward (north) along the Euphrates.
steps.simpleTranslation: Upward along the Euphrates, until where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the northern border on the other river, the Euphrates. Three answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as before, now for the פרת.

phrases.english: Upward along the Euphrates, until where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Tigris to the Euphrates.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The northern border of בבל along the Euphrates.

steps.title: Three opinions on the Euphrates border
steps.stepSummary: רב: the fortress of תולבקני. שמואל: the bridge over the Euphrates. רבי יוחנן: the crossing at גיזמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: until the fortress of תולבקני. שמואל said: until the bridge of the Euphrates. רבי יוחנן said: until the crossing of גיזמא.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים each name a different northern border along the Euphrates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion places the line at a different landmark. Which one reaches farther north becomes the key point in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav said: Until the fortress of Tulbaknei.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עַד גִּישְׁרָא דְּבֵי פְרָת.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Until the bridge of the Euphrates.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: עַד מַעַבַּרְתָּ[א] דְגִיזְמָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Until the crossing of Gizma.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: fortress of תולבקני. שמואל: bridge of the Euphrates. רבי יוחנן: crossing of גיזמא.

steps.title: אביי cursed those who followed רב
steps.stepSummary: אביי (some say רב יוסף) cursed anyone who followed רב's border.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי, and some say רב יוסף, would curse [those who followed] רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that אביי, or רב יוסף, cursed people who relied on רב's border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He felt רב's line went too far north, letting families of doubtful lineage count as בבל. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another name for who said it)

phrases.aramaic: לָיֵיט אַבָּיֵי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף אַדְּרַב.
phrases.english: Abaye, and some say Rav Yosef, would curse over Rav's view.
phrases.notes: He did not curse רב himself; he cursed people who used רב's border in practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָיֵיט אַבָּיֵי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף אַדְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts strongly to רב's opinion from step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רב's Euphrates border was strongly rejected by אביי or רב יוסף.

steps.title: Why curse over רב but not שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why only those following רב were cursed, since שמואל's border seems to reach even farther.
steps.simpleTranslation: He cursed over רב, but not over שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled: if רב's border was too far, שמואל's should be even worse, so why curse only over רב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the Euphrates bridge is farther north than the fortress of תולבקני. If so, שמואל includes even more doubtful area than רב.

phrases.english: He cursed over Rav, but over Shmuel he did not curse?
phrases.notes: The puzzle assumes the bridge is farther north than רב's fortress, so שמואל's line is even wider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that only רב's view was cursed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's border seems to reach even farther north than רב's, so it should deserve the curse even more.

steps.title: All the more so over שמואל
steps.stepSummary: First answer: he cursed over רב, and all the more so over שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he cursed over רב, and all the more so over שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's first answer: the curse covered שמואל too; mentioning רב was enough because שמואל's case is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even רב's smaller area deserved a curse, then שמואל's larger area surely did. This keeps the assumption that the bridge is farther north.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָיֵיט אַדְּרַב, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: Rather, he cursed over Rav, and all the more so over Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָיֵיט אַדְּרַב, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Expanding the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only those following רב were cursed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those following שמואל were cursed even more; רב was mentioned because his view was the smaller one.

steps.title: The bridge was actually farther south
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: only רב's view was cursed, because the Euphrates bridge actually stood farther south than רב's fortress.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: really he cursed over רב and not over שמואל, because the Euphrates bridge stood farther down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer: the curse really was only over רב, because שמואל's bridge was actually south of רב's fortress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer drops the assumption from step 38 that the bridge was farther north. If the bridge stood lower down, שמואל's border is smaller than רב's, so only רב's view went too far.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces a second answer)
Really; in truth (keeps the original claim)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read the curse: either it covered שמואל 'all the more so,' or שמואל's bridge was really south of רב's fortress, so only רב's border went too far.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַדְּרַב לָיֵיט, אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל לָא לָיֵיט,
phrases.english: Really, he cursed over Rav and did not curse over Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: וְגִישְׁרָא דְּבֵי פְרָת לְתַתַּאיה הֲוָה קָאֵי.
phrases.english: and the bridge of the Euphrates stood farther down.
phrases.notes: Farther down the river means farther south, so שמואל's border was inside רב's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the factual assumption of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bridge was north of רב's fortress, so שמואל's border was wider.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bridge stood farther south, so שמואל's border was narrower and only רב's deserved the curse.
